描述_ZN: Page from Yueyanglou, Yuan, painted by Xia Yong, on silk with ink brush, 24.4 cm in length and 26.2 cm in width.　　There is no author's mark on this panel. On the upper right, in small, fly-headed script, 23 lines, "Record of Yueyang Tower". There is a seal of authenticated collection, "Tingxiang family collection of picture books". On the opposite side of the panel, the seal reads "A true appreciation of the life of Li Zoxian of Wudi". 　　Li Zuoxian's inscription on the opposite side reads: "Yueyang Lou is a delicate drawing, with flying pavilions and layers of eaves, without a trace of disorder, and the characters in the building are all in place, almost like ghost workers. On the inscription of Yueyang Tower, regular script, such as fly-headed mosquito feet, enough to make the Lou blind, I do not know how the author of the pen. Such calligraphy and painting, is the Song people's mastery, after the Yuan and Ming, has become "Guangling San" carry on. Ancient and modern people are not similar, that is, the art thing can be seen. Li Zuoxian knows." Inscription: "Zhupeng" seal.　　Yueyang Tower is located in the territory of present-day Hunan Province, and is said to have been first used as a military parade platform for training the naval division of Lu Su, a famous general of the Three Kingdoms, and is also famous for the popular "Record of Yueyang Tower" by Fan Zhongyan, a famous writer of the Northern Song Dynasty.　　The composition and technique of this painting is the same as that of the other painting "Yueyanglou" in the National Palace Collection, except that one is a folding fan and the other is a booklet. Its neat and fine line drawing can be said to be "as fine as a mosquito's eyelashes, comparable to ghost workers". This technique of drawing architecture with purely white ink brush has become extinct after the Yuan Dynasty, so much so that Li Zoxian of Qing Dynasty mistakenly thought that this picture was made by Song people.
